repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CbUb7TcZK1XUAddUmQ

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ba0ec7c92b3476951c7ef42898477b7efc7def53`
Local-runs: probe — text search of the rule matcher inside the installed Claude Code 2.1.328 bundle, nothing executed: no file in the repo states what a two-wildcard Bash rule matches
Scope: .claude/settings.json + none
Security-touching: yes
The diff widens what an agent session may run without a prompt: a commit, and a push to the remote.

### ① Derived judgments

- Net diff against `main`: one file, `.claude/settings.json`, 3 added and 1 removed. Two entries are appended to `permissions.allow` (85 to 87). `permissions.deny` (17 entries) and `hooks` are byte-identical. The file parses. Right as described.
- Nothing published moves: no package, schema, export, route or doc. The surface that moves is the agent permission surface, and this file is read by every session opened in the repo, PM seats and a session on a maintainer's own machine included, not card developers alone.
- Client-side enforcement that could restrain the two commands, read in the tree: none. The four Bash PreToolUse hooks (`guard-shared-stash`, `guard-process-kill`, `guard-main-checkout-bash`, `guard-tree-enum`) read neither `git commit` nor `git push`. No `deny` entry names Bash. `check-settings-deny-roster` asserts the `mcp__github__` deny set alone and, by its own header, does not read `allow`. So for whatever these two entries match, the entry is the whole client-side decision.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is right: the diff publishes nothing from any released package. The body carries `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, both right. `Check Changeset` concluded success.

### ③ Boundary flags

No card, so no dev flags and no `open_questions`. The PR body's claims stand in their place, each read against the tree:

- "the same `Bash(cmd *)` wildcard form as the file's other entries": true of the spelling, wrong of the effect for the push entry (M1).
- "The commit rule ... does not allow `git add`, reset or rebase": true of those commands (N1 for what rides after the message file).
- "The push rule matches by prefix": wrong on this head. It does not match the prefix command itself (M1). The body's own example, `git push -u origin claude/issue-1:main`, does not match either, for the same reason; the class it stands for matches as soon as any argument follows (S1).
- "What keeps `main` safe is its branch protection and merge queue": holds as read over REST with the session's credential. Ruleset `main` (id 12119582) is active on the default branch with `deletion`, `non_fast_forward`, `merge_queue`, `pull_request` and `required_status_checks`; `current_user_can_bypass` reads `never`. The bypass-actor list is not readable with this credential (it returns null), so the claim is established for the fleet identity and not for any other.
- "The `deny` roster is unchanged": true. "Deny entries and hooks still run first": true of precedence, and empty for these two commands (①).
- "`check-settings-deny-roster` passes on this head": its step lives in `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, which concluded success.
- SQL push-down: not applicable, the diff holds no query code.

Check-runs on the head at reading: `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Test Core`, `Test UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, the PR-body guards, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · source gates` and every `Lint ·` lane but one concluded success. `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` and the `Type Check ·` lanes `consumer gates` and `debt ledger` were still in progress, so the head is not green yet. No check concluded failure.

### ④ Design judgment

`.claude/settings.json`, judged against the ruling (commits and card-branch pushes run without an approval) and against its first consumer, `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` rule 1, which prescribes `git push -u origin BRANCH` on a branch named `claude/issue-N-slug`.

**M1 (must-fix) — the push entry does not match the bare card-branch push it exists for.** The matcher turns each `*` into "any run of characters" and makes a trailing space-plus-wildcard optional only when that wildcard is the pattern's ONLY one. `Bash(git push -u origin claude/issue-* *)` carries two, so it means: `git push -u origin claude/issue-`, any run, ONE SPACE, any run. `git push -u origin claude/issue-35401-slug` ends at the branch name and has no such space, so it is not matched and meets the same approval stop as before. What the entry does match is every spelling with a further argument after the branch. The file's other two-wildcard entries are `curl` lines that always carry trailing header arguments, which is why the same spelling works there and not here; `Bash(git commit -F *)` has one wildcard and is unaffected. The single-wildcard spelling `Bash(git push -u origin claude/issue-*)` matches the bare command and every longer one. That is read from the matcher, not run.

**S1 (should-fix) — where the push entry matches, it is not confined to a card branch.** Everything after `claude/issue-` is free text, on this head and equally after the M1 respelling. Matching forms include a second refspec (`git push -u origin claude/issue-1 HEAD:OTHER`, the same with a leading plus, or `:OTHER` to delete), `--force`, `--delete`, `--mirror`, `--tags`, a tag name, and `--no-verify`. Server side `main` alone is protected: the protected-branch listing returns `main` only, there is no tag ruleset, and no rule applies to `claude/issue-*`. For every other ref the prompt this entry removes was the last thing in front of rules that already bind every seat:
- Multi-agent discipline §3: never force-push a shared branch, never bare `--force`. `claude/issue-*` is every developer's branch, not the caller's own.
- Prime Directive 15: never push a version tag. `changeset-release/main`, the Version Packages head, is unprotected too.
- `.githooks/pre-push`, which `--no-verify` skips, and whose header names it the place card relations in commit messages are refused.

The body discloses the `:main` case and none of these. The reach is damage to refs, not a publish: the only `on: push` triggers in `.github/workflows/` are filtered to `main`. An allow wildcard cannot express "one refspec and no flag", so the entry cannot be narrowed by respelling it. What can hold the line is the file's own second mechanism: `permissions.ask` entries for the excess shapes (ask outranks allow), or a PreToolUse Bash guard in the shape of the four already registered. This closes by one of those in the tree, or by the maintainer's own word on the PR accepting the wider reach as stated here.

Nits:
- N1 (nit) — the commit entry's wildcard carries anything after the message file: `-a` (stages every tracked change, the work of `git add -u`), `--amend`, pathspecs, and `--no-verify`, which skips `.githooks/pre-commit`. All local and reversible, and the push hook still collects a deferred regeneration, so no effect on the contract; the body's "does not allow `git add`" is true of the command and silent on staging.
- N2 (nit) — each entry matches one spelling: `git commit -F FILE` (not `-m`, not `git -C DIR commit`, no flag before `-F`) and `git push -u origin BRANCH` (not a later bare `git push`, not `git push origin BRANCH`). `os-dev.md` names the push spelling and no commit spelling, and no instruction file teaches `git commit -F`, so a developer who spells either differently meets the same stop. A follow-up for the `os-dev.md` owner; that file is outside this diff, read and not reviewed.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-xmk6ug`
Reviewed-by: `isolated-l2-35443`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0c3601b1aa1ddfff2edcf1b7ac0a685dafeb6eda`
Local-runs: probe — text search of the rule matcher and the deny, ask, allow order inside the installed Claude Code 2.1.328 bundle, nothing executed: no file in the repo states either
Scope: .claude/settings.json + none
Security-touching: yes
The diff widens what an agent session may run without a prompt, and adds the rules that decide which push and commit forms still ask.

Delta review of the round-1 record on the prior head. Read: the net diff against `main` on this head, the rewritten PR body, the check-runs on this head.

### ① Derived judgments

- Net diff against `main`: one file, `.claude/settings.json`, 15 added and 1 removed. `permissions.allow` gains `Bash(git commit -F *)` and `Bash(git push -u origin claude/issue-*)` (85 to 87). A new `permissions.ask` list holds ten entries. `permissions.deny` (17) and `hooks` are byte-identical. The file parses.
- Order of decision, read in the bundle: a matching deny rule decides first, then a matching ask rule, then a matching allow rule. So an ask entry outranks the allow entry, as the body says.
- New since round 1: the nine push entries in `ask` begin `git push *`, so they read every `git push` in every session, not only the pushes the allow entry reaches (N3).

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and right: `skip-changeset`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. `Check Changeset` reads skipped on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

The rewritten body, claim by claim:

- "Ask takes precedence over allow": true (①).
- "including the bare form os-dev uses": true (M1 below).
- "It covers push with `--force`/`-f`, `--delete`/`-d` ...": `-d` is covered only when another argument follows it, and `-f` only when it starts its own token (S1).
- "... are all asked, so they cannot rewrite or delete another ref": not true on this head for the trailing `-d` (S1).
- Commit, "`--no-verify` is asked": true of the long form; `git commit` also spells it `-n`, which is not asked (N1).
- "`main` is also protected by its ruleset": true as read in round 1.
- "Other spellings ... still asks, as today": not exact for a push the ask list now catches (N3).
- "Unchanged: the `deny` roster and the hooks": true. "`check-settings-deny-roster` passes": its step lives in `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, still in progress at reading.
- "Contract review round 1 ... is on this PR": true, one comment naming the prior head.
- SQL push-down: not applicable.

Check-runs on this head at reading: `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Test Core`, `Test UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Check PR Size`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, the three scoped lint lanes, `Type Check · workspace` and `Type Check · debt ledger` concluded success. Four `Lint ·` lanes (`CI, release & engine gates`, `ESLint`, `docs & code guards`, `repo & tooling gates`) and two `Type Check ·` lanes (`consumer gates`, `source gates`) were still in progress. One `PR-body guards` run is cancelled and its sibling concluded success. No check concluded failure. The head is not green yet.

### ④ Design judgment

M1: closed. `Bash(git push -u origin claude/issue-*)` has one wildcard and does not end in space-plus-wildcard, so it means `git push -u origin claude/issue-` followed by any run, the empty run included. `git push -u origin claude/issue-35401-slug` matches. The allow-only guard the matcher applies to wildcard rules does not bite this pattern.

Do the ask entries catch the plain card push? No. Each was read as the matcher compiles it against `git push -u origin claude/issue-1-fix-foo`:
- `* -f*` and `* -d *` need a space directly before the dash. A branch name holds no space, so `-fix-foo` or `-d` inside a slug is never caught.
- `*:*` needs a colon and `* +*` a space then a plus. A ref name can hold no colon, and the bare push has neither.
- `*--force*`, `*--delete*`, `*--mirror*`, `*--tags*`, `*--no-verify*` would need the slug itself to carry the double-dash word.
- `git commit *--no-verify*` does not touch `git commit -F FILE`.

One friction, in the safe direction: an ask wildcard is also tried against a whole chained or piped line, so a line that starts with the push and carries a colon or one of those flags anywhere later asks.

**S1 (should-fix) — kept, narrowed: one ask entry misses its own form, and a plain second refspec still rides.**
- `Bash(git push * -d *)` carries two wildcards, so its trailing space-plus-wildcard is not optional: the same trap as M1. git accepts options after the refspecs, and `git push -u origin claude/issue-999-other -d` ends at `-d`. It matches the allow entry and no ask entry, so it deletes that remote card branch with no prompt. No ruleset covers `claude/issue-*`. `Bash(git push * -d*)`, spelt like its `-f` sibling, catches both positions and still cannot catch a slug.
- Not reached by any ask entry, all inside the allow entry's reach. The first is the ordinary spelling; the rest are read from git's documented option parsing, not run:
  - a further plain refspec: `git push -u origin claude/issue-1 OTHER` creates or fast-forwards another ref, and `v1.2.3` or `tag v1.2.3` pushes a tag (Prime Directive 15; no tag ruleset);
  - `--follow-tags`;
  - `--prune` with a pattern refspec, which deletes;
  - a bundled short flag (`-qf`, `-qd`);
  - a unique long-option prefix (`--del`, `--mir`, `--no-veri`).
- An enumerated list cannot close that class. One entry can: `Bash(git push -u origin * *)` asks whenever anything follows the first refspec, leaving the bare push as the only promptless form. Its price is a prompt on a push line that is chained or piped.
- This closes with the `-d` entry respelt, and the rest either asked or stated in the body for the maintainer to accept by his own merge.

Nits:
- N1 (nit) — narrowed. The body now states `-a`, `--amend` and pathspecs. `git commit -F FILE -n` is the short spelling of `--no-verify` and is not asked. Local, and the push hook still collects.
- N2: closed for this PR. The body states that other spellings still stop. The `os-dev.md` follow-up stands.
- N3 (nit) — the nine push ask entries reach every `git push` in every session. `--force-with-lease=BRANCH:SHA`, the only force form Multi-agent discipline §3 permits, and any `SRC:DST` push now ask by rule wherever they are typed. The bundle's own text says that a run where nobody can be asked denies such a call. That may be exactly what is wanted; "still asks, as today" does not say it. Prefixing the entries `git push -u origin claude/issue-*` would confine them to the allow entry's reach.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-xmk6ug`
Reviewed-by: `isolated-l2-35443`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1255c914abf397e007f5340814f2f6ab6d976a31`
Local-runs: probe — text search of the rule matcher, the deny, ask, allow order and the command analysis inside the installed Claude Code 2.1.328 bundle, nothing executed: no file in the repo states them
Scope: .claude/settings.json + none
Security-touching: yes
The diff widens what an agent session may run without a prompt, and adds the rules that keep every longer form of those two commands asking.

Second delta, on the record for the prior head. Read: the net diff against `main` on this head, the rewritten PR body, the check-runs on this head.

### ① Derived judgments

- Net diff against `main`: one file, `.claude/settings.json`, 8 added and 1 removed. `permissions.allow` gains `Bash(git commit -F *)` and `Bash(git push -u origin claude/issue-*)` (85 to 87). A new `permissions.ask` list holds three entries. `permissions.deny` (17) and `hooks` are byte-identical. The file parses.
- As the matcher compiles them:
  - allow, commit: `git commit -F`, then nothing or a space and any run.
  - allow, push: `git push -u origin claude/issue-` and any run.
  - ask, commit: `git commit -F `, any run, ONE SPACE, any run.
  - ask, push: `git push -u origin claude/issue-`, any run, ONE SPACE, any run.
  - ask, refspec: `git push -u origin claude/issue-`, any run, a colon, any run.
- Order of decision, as read in delta 1: deny, then ask, then allow.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and right: `skip-changeset`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`.

### ③ Boundary flags

The rewritten body, claim by claim:

- "only the bare forms run without approval. Ask takes precedence over allow": true.
- "Runs without approval: exactly `git commit -F FILE` and `git push -u origin claude/issue-BRANCH`": true when either is typed as its own command. At the head of a chained or piped line it asks (N4).
- "the forms os-dev uses": true of the push; `os-dev.md` names no commit spelling (the N2 follow-up).
- "Still asks: anything after the message file ..., anything after the card branch ..., and a `src:dst` refspec": true, each checked in ④.
- "a message file path containing a space also asks": true.
- "every rule starts with the allowed command's own prefix, so no push or commit outside these two forms changes behaviour": true of the prefixes; the one exception is the chained line of N4.
- "Unchanged: `main`'s ruleset, the `deny` roster and the hooks": true.
- "`check-settings-deny-roster` passes locally": its CI step lives in `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, still in progress at reading.
- "The contract review records (round 1, delta 1) are on this PR": true, two comments.
- SQL push-down: not applicable.

Check-runs on this head at reading: `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Test Core`, `Test UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Check PR Size`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` and the three scoped lint lanes concluded success. Four `Lint ·` lanes (`CI, release & engine gates`, `ESLint`, `docs & code guards`, `repo & tooling gates`) and all four `Type Check ·` lanes were still in progress. One `PR-body guards` run is cancelled and its sibling concluded success. No check concluded failure. The head is not green yet, and this record does not stand in for those conclusions.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

M1: closed. The bare `git push -u origin claude/issue-35401-slug` matches the allow entry and neither push ask entry: after `claude/issue-` it holds no space and no colon. The bare `git commit -F FILE` matches its allow entry and not its ask entry: one token follows `-F`, so there is no second space.

S1: closed. Every form the two earlier records listed now meets an ask entry before the allow entry is read:
- a further refspec, a tag name or `tag NAME`, `--follow-tags`, `--prune` with a pattern, a bundled `-qf` or `-qd`, a long-option prefix such as `--del`, a trailing `-d`, `--force` in any spelling, `--no-verify`: each puts a space after the branch token, so the push ask entry matches;
- `claude/issue-1:main` and any other `SRC:DST` on the card token: the refspec ask entry matches with no space needed;
- `git commit -F FILE` followed by `-n`, `--no-verify`, `-a`, `--amend` or a pathspec: the commit ask entry matches.

What is left inside the allow entries' reach with no ask entry is one token and nothing else. For the push that is a single refspec beginning `claude/issue-`, with no colon, pushed without force through the pre-push hook: it creates or fast-forwards the remote branch of that name. That is any card branch, not only the caller's own, which is what the ruling's words cover. For the commit it is the message file. Shell operators cannot ride in the token: a chained line is split and each command is judged alone for allow. Brace expansion inside the token is refused as unanalysable before any rule is read, so it asks.

Nits:
- N1: closed. `-n` now asks.
- N2: closed for this PR. The `os-dev.md` follow-up stands: that file names no commit spelling.
- N3: closed. All three ask entries begin with their allow entry's own literal.
- N4 (nit) — an ask wildcard is also tried against a whole chained or piped line. A line that BEGINS with either allowed form and continues, such as the commit followed by a chained push, or the push piped into `tail`, asks by rule. A trailing stderr redirect alone should not, since rules are tried against the command with its redirections removed; I did not trace that step to its end. The asking is the safe direction and matches the fleet's own reading that a refused compound is retried as bare actions (`platform-readings.md`), but the body's "exactly" and "no ... changes behaviour" lines do not say it, and a developer has to know to type each command alone.
- N5 (nit) — not settled from the bundle: an unquoted variable or command substitution completing the branch or file token could word-split into further arguments at run time while the typed text holds no space. The analysis that refuses brace expansion sits in the same place, and I did not establish what it does with those two shapes. It is the deliberate-evader shape the repo's own Bash guards leave open by declared choice.

**VERDICT: PASS**
